page: Amazon Web Services m7g.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V1 CPU model running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and the system operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7g.4xlarge demonstrates strong memory performance, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score in the top 10% and a strong uncached large-block write memory bandwidth of 99.53 GB/sec. CPU performance is generally average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 12646.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 24503.85. However, the instance exhibits a relative weakness in cryptographic operations, scoring in the bottom 25% for the PassMark CPU encryption test, which is a notable tradeoff for security-heavy workloads.

For application workloads, the instance achieves average performance across database operations, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning tasks. It handles Redis SET operations at 26.37 million operations per second and static web serving at 29.33 GB/sec. Large language model inference with a 7B model shows average text generation speeds of 15.98 tokens per second, though prompt processing for the same model is relatively weak at 28.21 tokens per second. This profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and caching layers that benefit from high memory bandwidth without requiring local SSD storage.
